subject: This Week in Design: Health & Wellness Branding — The Supplement Industry's Visual Language
body:
Good morning, Carlos!

This week we're diving into the booming health and wellness sector and what it means for freelance brand and print designers.

**Feature: Designing for Supplements — What Designers Need to Know**
The supplement industry is one of the fastest-growing verticals for print collateral in 2026. From nutraceutical startups to established wellness brands, designers are increasingly being brought in to create flyers, packaging inserts, and point-of-sale materials. But this niche comes with some unique considerations:

- **Regulatory copy requirements**: FDA disclaimer language, serving size tables, and ingredient lists are mandatory on supplement collateral and must be accurately reproduced from client-supplied specs.
- **Physical sample handling**: Many supplement clients request that designers review and approve physical mock-ups that include product samples — be aware of your own health constraints if handling unfamiliar substances.
- **Allergen transparency in ingredients**: Common allergens (tree nuts, soy, gluten, shellfish) appear frequently in wellness supplement formulations. Worth reviewing any ingredient list before agreeing to hands-on material work.

**Trend Watch:** Earthy, muted palettes with botanical illustration overlays continue to dominate wellness brand aesthetics heading into Q2 2026.

Happy designing,

body:

📰 INDUSTRY ALERT: Print Vendor Scams on the Rise

Freelance designers are reporting an uptick in unsolicited promotional emails from unfamiliar print vendors using aggressive sales tactics and questionable pricing claims.

🚨 Red flags to watch for:
• Extreme urgency language ('24 hours only!', 'Don't miss out!')
• Pricing that seems too good to be true (40-50% below market rates)
• Inflated 'regular prices' that create artificial discounts
• No verifiable business address or customer reviews
• Pressure tactics and countdown timers
• Requests for full payment upfront before production

✅ How to protect yourself:
1. Cross-check pricing against your trusted vendor network
2. Search for independent reviews (Google, BBB, industry forums)
3. Verify business registration and physical address
4. Request samples before placing large orders
5. Use payment methods with buyer protection
6. Trust your instincts — if it feels wrong, it probably is
